liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Eyes Of The World** (3 reviews): Jerry keeps teasing the opening for a long time before finally getting into the first verses; Eyes has a sweet, long intro and is a highlight of a strong second set [8][11][13]
- **The Music Never Stopped** (1 review): The opening Music Never Stopped is described as tight [14]
- **Looks Like Rain** (1 review): Bob and Donna slow to Jerry's pace for a nice Looks Like Rain [15]
- **Cassidy** (1 review): Cassidy is also a nice version, played at the relaxed pace Bob and Donna set [15]
- **Mission In The Rain** (1 review): Reviewer says Mission In The Rain is well worth several listens [17]
- **Saint Stephen** (1 review): The Saint Stephen into Not Fade Away stretch rocks, after a first set that only picks up around Brown Eyed Women [8]
- **The Wheel** (1 review): Reviewer thinks this is the first Wheel placed after Drums, and says Deadbase agrees [11]

## Setlist highlights

- **Mission In The Rain**: rare: 5 archived performances [19]

## The recordings

- **gd1976-06-18.aud.vernon.9796.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 21 songs; 166 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [1]. Said about its sound: Phil and Jerry's interplay comes through clearly, capturing the Capitol Theater's acoustics on the audience recording [13]
- **gd76-06-18.warburton.vernon.14449.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 21 songs; 170 min; rated 3/5 by 8 [2]. Said about its sound: Audience recording sound quality is not great, though the reviewer finds the material excellent; Audience copy has fairly constant distortion and hiss, but the sound is consistent enough to enjoy; Somewhat muffled in places, but listenable and enjoyable overall [7][10][11][12]
- **gd1976-06-18.165169.sony.ecm99.warburton.wagner.miller.t-flac1644**: source not stated; 21 songs; 168 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [3]
- **gd1976-06-18.155902.ecm99.warburton.miller.flac2496**: source not stated; 21 songs; 168 min; rated 2/5 by 2 [4]
- **gd1976-06-18.aud.jackson.13052.shnf**: audience recording; 21 songs; 155 min [5]. Said about its sound: Noise reduction removed much of the hiss, but the recording remains somewhat muddy while still conveying live energy [5]

## Around the show

- Tickets for these shows were sold only through the Deadhead organization, by mailing a certified check and requested nights [7]
- Outside the theater, scalpers asked $60 and up, and few tickets were available [7]
- The Capitol was promoter Scher's home turf, and shows there were events; some tickets were sold through the band's newsletter [14]
- David Kreh and Jerry Moore were at the show, per the reviewer [18]
- Short second set; judged weaker than the Boston and Beacon shows from the same tour [8]
- Not among the top five shows of this strong tour, but still worth collecting, with Stephen into Eyes [14]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1976-06-18.aud.vernon.9796.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Dave Minor and Matt Vernon; source: ACM>C>DAT>CDR [1]
- **gd76-06-18.warburton.vernon.14449.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Jimmy Warburton; transferred by David Minches; source: Audience Recording: Sony ECM 99's [2]. Also: A soundboard version of this show is being released as Vol. 4 of the GD Download Series; Reviewer is listening to the officially released version of this show; Recorded with Sony ECM 99 microphones into a Sony TC-152 MC, then a Teac 2300 reel deck at 3.75 ips [2][10][15]
- **gd1976-06-18.165169.sony.ecm99.warburton.wagner.miller.t-flac1644**: taped by Recorded by Jimmy Warburton (30-35 rows right center); transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  February 24, 2022; source: (FOB) Sony ECM-99 > Cassette Master (Sony TC-152) > Cassette (Maxell UDXLI-C90) [3]. Also: This release is a conversion of the 2496 transfer (155902) down to 16-bit/44.1 FLAC [3]
- **gd1976-06-18.155902.ecm99.warburton.miller.flac2496**: taped by Jimmy Warburton; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  February 24, 2022; source: (FOB) Sony ECM-99 > Cassette Master (Sony TC-152) > Cassette (Maxell UDXLI-C90) [4]. Also: Reviewer says they taped this recording themselves [18]
- **gd1976-06-18.aud.jackson.13052.shnf**: transferred by Seth Jackson; source: Aud3>CDR>EAC>Pristine Sounds>SHN [5]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Capitol Theatre - June 19, 1976](https://www.dead.net/show/june-19-1976) [20]
